title: Focusing Forward
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Drawing on the image of driving between narrow barriers, where a driver who stares at the obstacles steers into them, the author argues that attention shapes action and that people achieve more when they fix on the destination rather than the surrounding noise. Focus is presented as a limited resource that determines what we perceive and do. Concentrating on the endpoint aligns behavior unconsciously, surfaces opportunities, builds confidence, and creates momentum with each milestone. The author frames forward focus as a learnable discipline used by the most accomplished leaders and performers.
points: Where we direct attention largely determines our experience and our actions, much as a driver's hands follow their eyes.
Dwelling on obstacles and distractions derails goals, while focusing on the endpoint helps us notice relevant opportunities.
Narrowing attention to a specific target raises confidence and makes execution more fluid, with each milestone compounding commitment.
Forward focus is a skill and discipline that top performers practice daily on both big and small goals.
quotes: Where we focus our attention significantly shapes our experience. Focus is a limited resource. Our perceptions and experiences are largely dictated by what we choose to pay attention to and focus on.
People achieve more when they focus on where they want to go and not on the noise that surrounds them. Both short- and long-term goals benefit from this forward focus.

Losing focus on the prize is what derails accomplishment and success. Distractions impede progress. While it is not always possible to block out the peripheral noise, the better we do at concentrating on the endpoint, the more we achieve.

We begin to see opportunities that might help us in our journey. Our heightened awareness reinforces the need to zero in on the details and milestones critical to success. Good things begin to happen.

As the impact of distractions lessens, our confidence rises. With a narrow scope aimed at a specific target, our execution becomes more fluid. With each passing milestone, the momentum of success builds and increases our commitment.
Focusing forward is a skill and a discipline, and the most productive and highly accomplished performers and leaders have mastered it. They use it every day with big and small goals. So should you.
